scope.scopeRationale: Only explicit EHI documentation is the carecloud prime PDF, which defines a CCDA + PDF non-clinical + undocumented FHIR Bulk mention. Scope therefore centers on that mixed artifact set.

sources.title: CareCloud EHI export PDF
sources.stabilityNotes: Single PDF artifact with version label but minimal changelog.
sources.sampleCoverageNotes: No example export files shipped with report.

sources.title: CareCloud Prime landing page screenshot
sources.stabilityNotes: Screenshot validates that EHI PDF is buried in marketing page footer.

sources.title: EHI link location screenshot
sources.stabilityNotes: Supports link discovery context and evidence of documentation location.

sources.title: EHI research narrative
sources.stabilityNotes: Captured summary with screenshots and structure-level mapping, no additional artifacts found.
sources.sampleCoverageNotes: No exports linked in this source.

items.quote: EHI PDF is linked from a marketing landing page under a Real World Testing heading.
items.relevance: Confirms evidence source and discoverability context.

assessmentFlow.method: Located PDF through registered URL and captured the actual marketing context and static evidence links.
observations: No additional public API documentation was found for the same registered URL.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Reduced confidence from governance and navigation perspective, not from data model alone.

items.quote: Clinical sections are described with XPATH and code-system mappings in dictionary tables.
items.relevance: Shows substantial documentation for clinical portion.

assessmentFlow.method: Parsed clinical CCDA dictionary and non-clinical section list to infer intended domain surface.
observations: Clinical model is reasonably mature, while non-clinical is intentionally undocumented.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Became a mixed-confidence hybrid export model.

items.quote: Insurance, appointments, billing claim data, provider-patient messages, and documents are exported in PDF format only.
items.relevance: Identifies major interoperability constraint.

assessmentFlow.method: Classified each documented export pathway by format and structuredness from PDF tables and narrative.
observations: Only partial standardization exists, and non-clinical data is non-computable as delivered.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Pulled operational conformance score down despite decent clinical dictionary detail.

items.quote: FHIR Bulk Data EHI Export is acknowledged as a one-sentence note with no details.
items.relevance: No usable evidence for standards-based full-export path.

gaps: No endpoint, resource list, or profile provided.

assessmentFlow.method: Compared clinical dictionary completeness against undocumented FHIR reference and PDF-only non-clinical exports.
observations: Potentially full EHI claim is not supported by documented non-clinical formats.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Supports hybrid projection classification with high manual effort for non-clinical data.

items.quote: Clinical coverage is reasonable; computability and completeness for non-clinical workflows are weak.
items.relevance: Confirms final rubric direction.

assessmentFlow.method: Set final scores favoring hybrid projection and moderate confidence with explicit missing-data and workflow risks.
observations: No sample files precludes deeper mapping validation.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Final classification: hybrid projection with substantial non-clinical limitations.

items.quote: CCDA XML is used for clinical data; non-clinical exports are in PDF; FHIR is only named without details.
items.relevance: Defines mixed container and serialization model.

gaps: No evidence on links between CCDA XML files and PDFs for one coherent recipient dataset.

exportSurface.accessibilityNotes: Report says exports can be run via UI with no developer dependency and any time access for admins.

items.quote: Clinical export is C-CDA XML while non-clinical is PDF, with undocumented FHIR mention.
items.relevance: Clear evidence of partial projection strategy.

gaps: No schema for non-clinical PDF and no usable FHIR endpoint details.

lossOrConflationExamples: PDF-only billing and appointments lose structured semantics for downstream migration systems.
Potential duplication or orphaning due undocumented linkage across CCDA and PDF outputs.
suspectedOmissions: Detailed non-clinical field maps for billing and insurance
Operationally usable FHIR export interface details

items.quote: Demographics, conditions, allergies, labs, vitals, procedures, medications, encounters, immunizations documented in clinical sections.
items.relevance: Explicit clinical section coverage.

domainAssessments.rationale: Core demographics are detailed via mapped CCDA section and XPATH references.

items.quote: Problems and diagnosis mapping is explicitly called out with SNOMED/ICD10 references.
items.relevance: Strong explicit problem-domain evidence.

domainAssessments.rationale: Problem/care continuity data has explicit field and coding context.

items.quote: Medications are covered with RxNorm/NDC and instruction fields via CCDA section dictionary.
items.relevance: Clinical medication completeness is relatively strong.

domainAssessments.rationale: Medication field structure is explicitly declared.
caveats: E-prescribing workflow history may remain partially represented.

items.quote: Laboratory tests/results appear with LOINC codes and interpretation fields.
items.relevance: Clinical lab evidence is explicitly present.

domainAssessments.rationale: Solid clinical test-level representation in CCDA dictionary.

items.quote: Vitals are represented via observations with standard code systems.
items.relevance: Clinical measurement coverage is present.

domainAssessments.rationale: Vascular and observational data are present in clinical dictionary.

items.quote: Insurance and billing are listed as PDF exports with no structural field definitions.
items.relevance: Domain present but low computable quality.

domainAssessments.rationale: Presence is confirmed but no dictionary/schema-level detail exists in public evidence.
caveats: Recipient systems cannot rely on these PDFs for automated ingestion.

items.quote: Appointments and provider-to-patient messages are mentioned as PDF outputs only.
items.relevance: Administrative workflow data is exported but not machine-friendly.

domainAssessments.rationale: Domain is covered by format only, not by schema depth.
caveats: No record-level field definitions or identifiers were provided.

items.quote: Billing data is represented as CPT/ICD/modifier in one-sentence coverage note.
items.relevance: Billing domain appears non-computable.

domainAssessments.rationale: Billing is present but with no export shape or fields.
caveats: Not suitable for machine extraction without custom OCR.

items.quote: Care plan and goals are documented in clinical CCDA sections.
items.relevance: Demonstrates meaningful care-plan coverage.

domainAssessments.rationale: Care plan data exists in clinical section dictionary, with moderate implementation clarity.
caveats: Detailed value structure for all goal state transitions is not explicit.

items.quote: Signed notes, lab/radiology/scanned documents are exported in PDF with no field-level schema.
items.relevance: Document attachment coverage is broad but not machine-computable.

domainAssessments.rationale: Existence is strong but interoperability is weak due PDF-only representation.
caveats: No explicit linkage keys or machine-consumable metadata in provided docs.

items.quote: Messages are listed as a PDF export type only.
items.relevance: Communication coverage is present only at document level.

domainAssessments.rationale: Exists in principle but unstructured, limiting reliable downstream ingestion.
caveats: No schema for message headers, threads, or attachments.

items.quote: Clinical coverage is strong but administrative and billing exports are non-computable.
items.relevance: Scope is uneven across clinical and operational modules.

dimensionScores.rationale: Core clinical domains are broad; PM/financial/admin areas are represented only partly.
dimensionScores.uncertaintyNotes: Could improve with PDF schema and additional appendices.

items.quote: One export uses structured XML and another uses PDF with no computable dictionary.

dimensionScores.rationale: CCDA is stable/standard; PDF outputs are not suitable for automated ingestion.
dimensionScores.uncertaintyNotes: Overall openness limited by non-clinical payload shape ambiguity.

items.quote: Clinical dictionary includes XPATH, OIDs, and code-system names in multiple sections.
items.relevance: Strong field documentation for structured part.

gaps: PDF portions have no schema-level definition.

dimensionScores.rationale: Hybrid quality: high for clinical CCDA, low for non-clinical sections.
dimensionScores.uncertaintyNotes: A single dictionary for PDF exports would materially improve this score.

items.quote: UI screenshots show self-service selection and export triggers.
items.relevance: Accessibility is operationally better than documented APIs in practice.

dimensionScores.rationale: Self-service UI path is described and consistent with no developer onboarding requirement.
dimensionScores.uncertaintyNotes: Institutional roles/permissions can still gate actual use.

items.quote: Some data remains in PDF or undocumented FHIR mention, which is not direct internal-to-standards reflection.

dimensionScores.rationale: Clinical model fidelity is moderate-high, while non-clinical fidelity is limited by non-machine formats.
dimensionScores.uncertaintyNotes: FHIR details could significantly change this if fully documented.

items.quote: Data semantics are lost or hidden when compressed into PDF views.
items.relevance: Projection risk due format collapse.

dimensionScores.rationale: Projection risk is mainly due non-computable administrative export formats.
dimensionScores.uncertaintyNotes: CCDA side is lower-risk; overall remains elevated due PDFs.

items.quote: Two formats can collapse domain distinctions unless explicitly linked, and some workflows are only mentioned.
